memo.verdict: Neutral; park. Clariant (CLN-CH) at CHF 10.67 (close 2026-09-25) is a cause-for-concern-clearing case with a self-help engine underneath it, fair at this price and compelling at about CHF 9.35. The record does not progress it and does not invalidate it. Two re-entry triggers: a price at or below CHF 9.35 with the case intact (which restores the framework's B anchor of about 20 percent a year on the modal path), or a German procedural or first-instance court step that follows the Amsterdam reasoning (which moves the case to its cleared branch). One date: the Q3 2026 print on 3 November 2026, which decides the Catalysts leg. Conviction medium: the litigation odds are a working hypothesis, the operating odds are evidenced. The park rule does not fire (management B, business quality C, predictability C, trackability C); the park is on the return and the setup, not on the gate. Primary 'Target Setup' 'Major CfC Clearing', fit C; secondary 'Major Corporate Change', fit C. Modal return about 10.0 percent a year over eighteen months and about 10.8 percent a year over three years, a D against the framework's anchors.
case: The change forces. The largest force is external, legal and half-cleared: the Amsterdam dismissal of 29 July 2026 is the first court test of follow-on ethylene-cartel claims that capped the valuation for four years, and about EUR 6.4 billion remains in German courts, unprovisioned, with Dow Europe's EUR 1.1 billion claim filed inside the clearing window. The other external forces are net headwinds turning at the margin (Middle East refill deferrals abating; European energy, Chinese specialty entry and the franc persisting), rated D as change forces because the tailwinds are the reversal of headwinds, not new demand; no force meets the 'Demand Inflection' test. The internal forces are real, measured and led by a strong operator but are the continuation of a programme begun in 2023: two of twelve strong (other leaders B; standards improvement B, with CHF 69m of CHF 100m banked, 52 percent cash conversion, governance repaired after the 2021 to 2022 restatement), six moderate, four absent or reversed (no chief-executive change; deleveraging rather than balance-sheet use; a flat CHF 0.42 distribution; no new geographies). The screen's rule is not met, so 'Change Forces' is C. Propagation: to the financial statements on margin and cash; to the sell-side since 31 July 2026; not to the revenue line.

The financial outputs. Margin B (14.6 percent in 2023 to 18.2 percent in Q2 2026; guided 19 to 21 percent by 2027; a third from self-help, two-thirds from volume that has not arrived). Cash conversion B (32 to 52 percent; leaning on working-capital release and deferred capex). Revenue C (from -5.7 percent to +3.7 percent by FY2027, below the 4 to 6 percent target and far below the 12 to 20 percent band). Net debt C (2.2x rising near term, set to fall). Sell-side upgrades likely but modest, C: the margin guide sits about 1 percent above consensus EBITDA of CHF 671m, the 2027 targets well above the FY2027 consensus margin of 18.4 percent, the post-results skew better than three to one (B), but the twelve-month history is deeply negative and the H2 2026 Catalysts recovery unproven; commentary split between Deutsche Bank's substantial upside and Bernstein's and Morgan Stanley's slippage to 2027. Our modal FY2026 EPS is about CHF 0.71, in line with guidance and consensus (no Viewforth model exists; our own estimate stands in). Goldilocks C: the eighteen-month rate (+22.6 percent FY2026 to FY2027) is just above the band in the fine-but-riskier zone, the bridge mostly identified (about CHF 22m of incremental savings, CHF 18m of Catalysts recovery, CHF 19m in Care Chemicals, less the CHF 8m revaluation reversal, against fixed D&A of about CHF 240m); the three-year rate (about 11 percent) just below; the six-month rate above 40 percent on a depressed base and marked down for return-to-base-rate risk. Staircase C: dated steps (3 November 2026; CHF 90m at year-end; February 2027 guide; CHF 100m run-rate; the 2027 target year; German court steps) that are milestones on a known path, the largest exogenous and undated. 'Financial Outputs' C: the eighteen-month growth is recovery, not compounding.

The return. Valuation convention: at each horizon the shares are valued at a multiple of the earnings two years beyond it. Today's 24-month-forward EPS is CHF 0.90 (dashboard CHF 0.8989), the multiple 11.9x (11.86x). Eighteen months out (March 2028) the 24-month-forward EPS is CHF 0.99 (three-quarters of FY2029 CHF 0.97 plus a quarter of FY2030 CHF 1.04); at 12.0x, the uncleared-and-delivering modal branch, plus a CHF 0.42 dividend, the total is CHF 12.30, +15.3 percent, 10.0 percent a year (factors: earnings 1.100, re-rating 1.012, cash 1.035; product 1.152); at the blended 11.9x, CHF 12.20, 9.3 percent a year. Three years out (September 2029) the figure is CHF 1.08 (a quarter of FY2030 and three-quarters of FY2031 CHF 1.10); at the blended 12.2x plus CHF 1.33 of dividends, CHF 14.51, +36.0 percent, 10.8 percent a year (factors 1.200, 1.029, 1.101; product 1.359). Branches and odds at eighteen months: cleared 23 percent at 13.5x; uncleared and delivering 55 percent at 12.0x; uncleared and stalled 10 percent at 10.5x; adverse ruling 12 percent at 9.5x; blend 11.9x. At three years: cleared 45 percent, uncleared 35 percent, adverse 20 percent; blend 12.2x. The 12.0x anchor sits between the five-year median (11.49x) and the ten-year 35th percentile (12.10x) because the five-year window embeds the litigation discount and the ten-year window includes the pre-2020 premium years (Clariant then at a 26 percent premium to peers). Conceded floors: the ten-year median 13.4x is fair for a cleared Clariant (the cleared branch at 13.5x gives CHF 13.79, +29 percent, 18.6 percent a year); the peer median 14.0x gives CHF 14.28, 21.4 percent a year and clears the bar, but is not used because the peers above the median earn above their cost of capital and the closest business peers (Evonik 12.4x, Arkema 9.5x) sit below. One-year-forward footing: 12.9x on CHF 0.83 now; CHF 0.93 at eighteen months; CHF 12.46, 10.9 percent a year; the convention moves a point, not the answer. Drop-through sensitivity: tax and minorities at 35 percent instead of 32.8 percent and interest CHF 10m higher take FY2029 EPS from CHF 0.97 to CHF 0.92 and FY2030 from CHF 1.04 to CHF 0.98; the eighteen-month figure CHF 0.935; the total CHF 11.64, +9.1 percent, 6.0 percent a year, an F; combined with a Catalysts shortfall (FY2029 EBITDA CHF 760m instead of CHF 800m) about 2 percent a year; 'Modal return' D falls to F and 'Investment Thesis' C to D on the adverse ratio; the modal path is the D. Parts add up: from FY2028 consensus (revenue CHF 4,079m, EBITDA CHF 774m, EPS CHF 0.92) to FY2031 on our path (CHF 4,450m, CHF 862m at 19.4 percent, EPS CHF 1.10): revenue +3.0 percent a year, margin +0.7 percent, below-EBITDA gearing +2.3 percent, share count 0; product 1.061, +6.1 percent a year, matching EPS +19.6 percent over three years. Components in the order investors reward least: little from revenue, a fair amount from margin, most of the gearing from fixed D&A and interest, nothing from buybacks (328.9m shares, unchanged since FY2019). Dividends B: 3.9 percent yield, covered 2.1 times by FY2026 consensus free cash flow, held through the FY2025 loss year, flat. Re-rating C: room to 13.4x and to 14.0x exists, but is earned by a German court or the 2027 margin, neither in the company's gift inside eighteen months; the re-rating that was ours (8.9x to 11.9x) has happened. Already priced: the Amsterdam ruling and the Q2 beat, yes; a German ruling either way, no; the crisp entry was at CHF 7 to 8 and the park has moved against us by about 40 percent. The price that clears the bar: CHF 9.35 over eighteen months, CHF 8.40 over three years. 'Modal return' D.
counter_case: The strongest case against the neutral verdict is the bull case in Deutsche Bank's form (Buy, CHF 12.60, 23 September 2026, 40 percent upside), strengthened with the Catalysts timing argument. The market still discounts twice the litigation risk that is justified after Amsterdam: Deutsche Bank says the market prices CHF 343m against its own CHF 50m. The German claims rest on the same European Commission decision and the same economic record the Amsterdam court found could not show a price effect (the monthly contract price tracked naphtha; the defendants bought 14.6 percent of the market), the Stichting's parallel claim fell with Shell's, and the German courts are likely to follow. Clariant's EBITDA was the most stable in its European peer group through 2022 to 2025 (-8 percent a year against Evonik -9 percent and Arkema -16 percent); its cash conversion is top-decile at 52 percent; its 2027 free cash flow yield is 8.1 percent; and the 2027 targets (a 19 to 21 percent margin, 4 to 6 percent growth) are substantial upside to a consensus at 18.4 percent for FY2027. The deferred refills are maintenance that must happen, so FY2027 Catalysts EBITDA bounces above the CHF 164m of FY2025 rather than trickling to consensus CHF 146m, which alone adds about CHF 0.04 to FY2027 EPS. A business at 19 to 21 percent margins with the overhang gone re-rates to its pre-2020 premium of 26 percent to peers, above 14x, for a return above 25 percent a year; even at the peer median of 14.0x the eighteen-month return is CHF 14.28, 21.4 percent a year, and clears the bar. On this reading the 'Investment Thesis' is a B, the setup fit is a B if the trough condition is read against the ten-year window rather than the five-year, and the 'Investment Case' is a C, because a business with a B operator, a delivered cost programme, a legal precedent on its side and an early-Stage-2 chart is a C case wherever the multiple sits; the framework's counts penalise it for being mid-quality, not for being risky.

The record concedes the direction of the precedent, the quality of the cost and cash delivery, that its uncleared multiple of 12.0x sits below the ten-year median of 13.4x, that refills are deferred rather than lost, that the multiple is cheap against ten years and against peers, and that the counts are calibration rather than judgement. It holds because the bull case needs a German ruling inside the horizon (about 23 percent on the record's odds; Bernstein expects considerable time; the Dow claim was only served on 17 July 2026) or a return to 4 to 6 percent organic growth (not on the record of any year since 2022, against flat volumes, energy at 3.3 times United States prices and Chinese competitors moving up the chain); without one of them the bull case is the record's own cleared branch at 13.5x, 18.6 percent a year, one turn short of the premium multiple and one-in-four in probability. The refill bounce is a timing gain consensus already spreads over FY2027 and FY2028. The same court that can add CHF 1.5 to 2.0 a share can take CHF 2 to 3 off, a skew the price at CHF 10.67 does not pay for and the price at CHF 7 did. The trough condition is a threshold, not a spirit: bottom quartile is 9.14x on five years and below the 32nd percentile on ten, and 11.5x is neither. And the chosen setup's constraint was its trough multiple; without it the holder owns an unresolved EUR 6.4 billion docket, a refill cycle in the Middle East and China, and a multiple already paid for the good half of the news.
triggers: Re-entry triggers: a price at or below CHF 9.35 with the case intact (CHF 8.40 on the three-year horizon); a German procedural or first-instance step that follows the Amsterdam reasoning, which moves the case to the cleared branch at 13.5x; a settlement of the German claims at a small figure, which does the same at once.

Alarm levels: a German court declining to follow the Amsterdam reasoning at any procedural step (moves the odds to even and the uncleared multiple down toward 9.5x); Q3 2026 Catalysts sales below about CHF 170m on 3 November 2026; the savings run-rate below CHF 85m at December 2026; raw-material inflation above 10 percent; the 24-month-forward multiple above 13x without a ruling or below 10x; the FY2026 EBITDA margin below 17.5 percent; a 5 percent cut to FY2027 consensus EPS over three months; cash conversion below 40 percent; net debt to EBITDA above 2.5x; Chinese propane-dehydrogenation utilisation at 60 percent; FY2027 local-currency growth below 2 percent; EUR/CHF below 0.90; a fifth year of restructuring charges above CHF 30m; Lucas Meyer growth below 5 percent in a year; a change of chief executive or chief financial officer.

Invalidate levels: a first-instance German award against the defendants of any size; FY2026 Catalysts segment EBITDA below CHF 110m; the savings target cut; a Care Chemicals margin below 18 percent for two quarters; an FY2027 EBITDA margin below 18 percent; cash conversion below 30 percent for a year; a dividend cut; a missed margin guide; a Chinese-driven fall in Catalysts Asia sales for two consecutive quarters after H2 2026.

What would confirm the case: the Q3 2026 print showing the H2 Catalysts recovery and force majeures below 100 turning into orders (to 12.5x or more without a ruling); the December 2026 run-rate at CHF 90m; the February 2027 FY2027 guide putting a number on the 19 to 21 percent year; deleveraging below 2.0x opening the shareholder-returns question; the six-month revision figures turning positive by October and the F pin re-read at the next snapshot.

Open questions the record could not close: the Catalysts order book (not disclosed and not obtainable); the timing of any German first-instance ruling (undated; Munich and Dortmund dockets reported only through the sell-side or the company); whether Shell appeals in the Netherlands; the H1 2026 net income gap (CHF 85m in the research against CHF 70.3m reported in FactSet, unexplained, nowhere load-bearing); return on tangible capital (not computable without inventing a figure); the live thematics file, the ticker's sidecar, the track-record and lessons files and the Wisdom Library (not among the inputs read; the dependent items labelled); whether SABIC's 31.5 percent stake moves (nothing signalled either way; crossing 33.3 percent would trigger a mandatory offer). Leading indicators: sector force majeure counts, Chinese propane-dehydrogenation utilisation, the Europe-to-United States gas ratio, European ethylene and propylene contract prices, EUR/CHF and USD/CHF (a 1 percent move is CHF 4m of EBITDA), the German dockets, Care Chemicals customer inventories, the savings run-rate, consensus revisions weekly, peer prints (Croda Consumer Care, Evonik Custom Solutions, Honeywell catalyst aftermarket); the macro series monthly or better, the company series quarterly, the legal series event-driven.
